title: ～ごとに — every ～, at each ～
summary: Shows that the same thing repeats at each interval or unit. It follows a noun of time, place or unit, or the dictionary form of a verb.

body.p: After a noun it means 'for each one' or at every such interval: 駅ごと, 三日ごと. After a verb it means 'every time you ～' and often describes a change progressing.
毎～ names the cycle itself, while ～ごとに stresses that something happens at each unit. Be careful with ～おきに, which skips a unit: 一日おきに is every other day.

examples.ja: この電車（でんしゃ）は駅（えき）ごとに止（と）まります。
examples.romaji: Kono densha wa eki goto ni tomarimasu.
examples.tr: This train stops at every station.

examples.ja: 一（いち）ページごとに単語（たんご）の意味（いみ）を確認（かくにん）する。
examples.romaji: Ichi pēji goto ni tango no imi o kakunin suru.
examples.tr: I check the meaning of the words on each page.

examples.ja: 年（とし）を取（と）るごとに、時間（じかん）が早（はや）く過（す）ぎるように感（かん）じる。
examples.romaji: Toshi o toru goto ni, jikan ga hayaku sugiru yō ni kanjiru.
examples.tr: With each passing year, time seems to go by faster.

pitfalls: 一日おきに means every other day, while 一日ごとに means every day.
Use the dictionary form with verbs (取るごとに), not the past form.
